subquestions.prompt: Compute Kappa's standalone equity value, Omega's investment value for 100% of Kappa's equity, and Omega's NPV if it pays €12.50 per share. Round to one decimal.

questions.stem: Gamma SpA (Italy) is listed with a market capitalization of €900m. It has bonds with a face value of €500m trading at 92% of par (yield to maturity 5,5%), bank loans of €150m (book value), and cash of €50m. Last year's interest expense was €34m. It pays IRES of 24% on pre-tax profit and IRAP of 3,9% on EBIT plus personnel costs. The industry unlevered beta is 0,9, the risk-free rate 3% and the MRP 6%. Use net debt and the market cost of debt.

source.file: Slides/Corporate Valuation - C31 - Lecture 4 - Cost of Capital - v3.pdf
source.location: L4 slides 27–39 (tax rate, leverage, cost of debt, final choices)
source.label: INFERENCE

subquestions.prompt: Estimate the WACC relevering the industry beta and using the CAPM (option 2 in the slides).
Recompute the WACC with option 1 (unlevered cost of equity from the CAPM, then Modigliani & Miller's second proposition) and explain the difference.

answer_key.answer: WACC ≈ 7.63%: kEU 8.40%, kEL 9.77%. The two agree only if kD = rF; here kD 5,5% > rF 3%.

mark_scheme: [2] Steps: (1) kEU = 3% + 0,9 × 6% = 8.40%; (2) MM2: kEL = kEU + D/E × (kEU − kD) × (1 − t) = 9.771%; (3) same weights; (4) WACC = 7.627%; (5) difference 0.73 points; (6) cause: option 2's CAPM relevering treats debt as riskless (implicitly kD = rF); (7) they coincide only if kD = rF.
Not needed: book equity and last year's interest expense (the accounting kD), except as distractors.

citations.quote: Second portion of income taxes: ~ equal to 3,9% of (EBIT + personnel expenses)
Debt and equity should be measured with their market values
Option 1 = Option 2 when kD = rF !

questions.stem: Zeta SpA reports by function (€m): revenues 1.200; cost of goods sold 620 (including D&A of 40); SG&A 300 (including D&A of 20 and a one-off restructuring charge of 25); other operating income 15 (of which 12 is a gain on selling a non-core building); income from associates 8; interest expense 30; interest income 4; income taxes 70. subquestions.prompt: Recurring EBITDA and its margin, recurring EBIT and NOPAT (24% tax).
Rebuild EBT from recurring EBIT in the reorganized layout, showing the exceptional items, associates and net interest.

answer_key.answer: Recurring EBITDA 368 (30.7% of sales); EBIT 308; NOPAT 234.1.
EBT 277 = EBIT 308 − exceptional items 13 (−25 + 12) + associates 8 − net interest 26.

error_tags.trap: 1: restructuring charge and building gain left in EBITDA
1: D&A inside COGS and SG&A left in

mark_scheme: [1] Steps: (1) COGS excl. D&A = 580; (2) SG&A excl. D&A and the one-off = 255; (3) recurring other income = 3; (4) recurring EBITDA = 1.200 − 580 − 255 + 3 = 368; (5) margin = 30.67%; (6) D&A = 60; (7) EBIT = 308; (8) NOPAT = 308 × 0,76 = 234.08. questions.stem: An asset-side DCF gives Eta SpA an enterprise value of €5.000m. At the valuation date: net debt €1.400m; pension deficit €150m; a non-recurring long-term provision €60m; minorities €200m at market value (€90m book); preferred equity €100m; associates €250m at market value (€180m book); non-core real estate €120m. There are 200m common shares.

mark_scheme: [1] Steps: (1) start from EV 5.000; (2) − net debt 1.400; (3) − pension deficit 150 and − provision 60 (debt-like); (4) − minorities 200 and − preferred 100 (equity-like claims of others, at market value); (5) + associates 250 and + non-core real estate 120; (6) equity = 3460; (7) per share = 3460 / 200 = 17.30.
